(November 4, 2026) – Martin Marietta Materials, Inc. (NYSE: MLM) (Martin Marietta or the Company), a leading supplier of aggregates, lime and limestone products, magnesia-based products and other building materials, today reported results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. For additional notes, see page 14. 1 Ward Nye, Chair, President and CEO of Martin Marietta, stated, “Martin Marietta delivered record quarterly revenues of $2.37 billion and Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations of $808 million, representing increases of 28% and 21%, respectively, over the prior year third quarter, as strong performance from recent acquisitions more than offset the effects of expanding inflationary pressures and a dynamic macroeconomic environment. "The third quarter marked a defining milestone in Martin Marietta's portfolio transformation with the completion of our combination with Lhoist North America (LNA) on August 21. This transaction meaningfully scales our differentiated upstream Specialties platform, establishing Martin Marietta as the nation's leading producer of lime and limestone solutions and broadening our participation across steel, environmental, infrastructure and industrial end markets. Since the closing date, LNA delivered revenues, gross profit and cash gross profit 1 of $216 million, $51 million and $115 million, respectively, providing early validation of the strategic and financial merits of the higher-quality, more resilient and diversified portfolio we have intentionally built. With the closing of LNA, we have updated the midpoints of our full-year 2026 Revenue and Adjusted EBITDA guidance to $7.80 billion and $2.48 billion, respectively, as acquisition contributions are anticipated to more than offset lower near-term expectations for our heritage operations. In 2027, we expect mid- to high-single digit aggregates pricing on a mix-adjusted basis, supported by January 1 pricing actions designed to address inflationary cost pressures. Acquired operations, which currently have selling prices below the Company average, provide meaningful opportunity for continued pricing growth. From an end market perspective, we currently expect continued strength in infrastructure and data centers with softer interest rate-sensitive private construction markets." Mr. Nye concluded, "As we integrate this year’s acquisitions, we remain focused on safety, commercial and operational excellence, and disciplined execution of the matters within our control. Martin Marietta has a proven playbook for responding decisively to changing market conditions, managing inflationary pressures, protecting profitability and maximizing free cash flow. That playbook is already delivering results, with disciplined inventory management and capital spending reductions alone contributing over $290 million of year-to-date cash flow improvement. Looking ahead, January 1 pricing actions and further structural cost improvements are expected to restore a positive price-cost relationship in 2027. With today's broader end-market exposure and more resilient earnings profile, Martin Marietta is better positioned to navigate near-term uncertainty while capitalizing on the attractive long-term fundamentals of our business.” ﻿ 2 Third-Quarter Financial and Operating Results (All financial and operating results are for continuing operations and comparisons are versus the prior-year third quarter, unless otherwise noted) Building Materials Business Aggregates Third-quarter aggregates shipments increased 15.9 percent to a record of 67.1 million tons driven by acquisition contributions that more than offset a modest decline in organic shipments. ASP decreased 3.6 percent to $22.41 per ton, primarily reflecting acquisition-related mix, as acquired operations have average selling prices below the Company average. Organic ASP increased 1.0 percent, while organic mix-adjusted ASP 6 increased 2.7 percent. Aggregates gross profit decreased 4 percent to $512 million, primarily due to higher depreciation, depletion and amortization, and energy-related costs. Aggregates cash gross profit 1 , however, reached an all-time quarterly record of $696 million as acquisition contributions more than offset organic price-cost headwinds. Other Building Materials Other Building Materials revenues increased 14 percent to $399 million, and gross profit increased 17 percent to $63 million, benefiting from acquisition contributions and strong performance from the California asphalt business. Specialties Business Specialties delivered record revenues, gross profit and cash gross profit 1 of $362 million, $88 million and $163 million, respectively, reflecting strong organic performance and partial quarter contributions from LNA. Organic Specialties revenues and gross profit increased 11 percent and 6 percent, respectively. Portfolio Optimization On August 21, 2026, the Company completed the business combination with LNA, a leading producer of high-calcium lime, dolomitic lime and industrial mineral products serving diversified end markets through a network of 20 quarries and production facilities and 45 distribution terminals. On September 18, 2026, the Company acquired The Frazier Quarry, Inc., a pure-play aggregates business located in Harrisonburg, Virginia. Cash Generation, Capital Allocation and Liquidity Cash provided by operating activities for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, was $896 million compared with $1,156 million for the prior-year period. The year-over-year comparison includes $250 million of cash tax payments related to the gain recognized on the February 2026 QUIKRETE asset exchange. Cash paid for property, plant and equipment additions for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, was $445 million, compared with $602 million for the prior-year period. In July, the Company entered into a $1.5 billion three-year senior unsecured term loan facility and, in August, issued $5.5 billion of senior unsecured notes across five tranches to fund the cash consideration for the LNA 3 combination. On August 21, 2026, the Company completed the LNA combination for total consideration of $12.9 billion, consisting of $7.0 billion in cash and approximately $5.9 billion of Martin Marietta common stock. During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company returned $361 million to shareholders through dividend payments and share repurchases. As of September 30, 2026, 10.7 million shares remained available under the current repurchase authorization. As of September 30, 2026, the Company had $140 million of unrestricted cash and cash equivalents on hand and $1.4 billion of unused borrowing capacity under its existing credit facilities. For each respective product line, the Company calculates cash gross profit by adding back to gross profit the noncash charges for depreciation, depletion and amortization and the impact of selling acquired inventory after markup to fair value as part of acquisition accounting for that product line. Aggregates cash gross profit and Specialties cash gross profit are not defined by accounting principles generally accepted in the United States (GAAP) and, as such, should not be construed as alternatives to gross profit, the most directly comparable GAAP financial measure. For further information on aggregates cash gross profit and Specialties cash gross profit, refer to the Company’s website at www.martinmarietta.com .
